description: APCA 0.0.98G-4g. Every constant is pinned digit for digit at tolerance 0, and every Lc value is asserted BITWISE against colorjs.io's independent implementation of the same revision — worst difference across the set is exactly 0. APCA has been revised repeatedly, so the version is part of the answer: 'Lc 62' without a revision is not a reproducible claim.

entries.source: APCA (Myndex, apca-w3); colorjs.io's contrast/APCA.js carries the same revision
APCA 0.0.98G-4g — scaleBoW and scaleWoB are both 1.14; loBoWoffset and loWoBoffset are both 0.027 (w3c/silver issue 645)

entries.derivationNote: Background white, text black. The maximum positive Lc — dark text on a light background. Note it is NOT the magnitude of the reverse case: APCA is asymmetric by design.

Background black, text white. NEGATIVE by design — the sign carries the polarity, and taking the absolute value throws away half the answer. |-107.88| is also not 106.04: light-on-dark and dark-on-light are different perceptual problems with different exponents.

entries.source: APCA 0.0.98G-4g applied to the grey WCAG treats as the AA threshold against white
entries.derivationNote: sRGB [118,118,118] on white. WCAG rates this pairing 4.5422 — just passing AA. APCA rates it Lc 71.6, which is comfortably readable for body text. The two models agreeing here is why this pairing is uncontroversial.

entries.source: APCA 0.0.98G-4g applied to sRGB blue on white
entries.derivationNote: WCAG rates white-on-blue 8.59 — nearly twice its AA threshold, suggesting excellent contrast. APCA rates it Lc -90.7, also high. The interesting disagreements are elsewhere; this entry pins the pairing so a future change to either model shows the divergence moving. ADR-0021 sends any disagreement to design review rather than letting one model override the other.

White background, #FEFEFE text — one 8-bit step apart. Reports exactly 0 rather than a small number, because APCA declines to report a contrast nobody should act on. An implementation missing the gates returns roughly 0.5 here, which looks harmless and is a measurement that was not made.
